quote.text: For want of a naile the shoe is lost, for want of a shoe the horse is lost, for want of a horse the rider is lost.
quote.author: George Herbert, Outlandish Proverbs, 1640; the familiar longer version is Franklin’s, in Poor Richard’s Almanack, 1758

stories.kicker: Buy It Once · Pepper mills & salt grinders
stories.headline: The burr is the product. Everything else is a handle
stories.dek: A pepper mill is a cutting tool wearing a decorative body, and almost nobody sells you the cutting tool. Two test kitchens have now independently named a sixty-dollar mill best overall — and the two-hundred-dollar one carries the shortest warranty in the category.

stories.kicker: Down the Rabbit Hole · Urban sketching & watercolour
stories.headline: The proof is that you were there
stories.dek: A movement that began as a Flickr group in 2007 has passed five hundred and ninety-nine chapters. Its founding document is eight sentences long, and the first of them — draw from direct observation, on location — has turned out to be a rule about authenticity that nobody in 2007 knew they were writing.

stories.headline: The trophy and the loss arrived in the same quarter
stories.dek: Singapore Airlines was named the world’s best airline again on Friday, by 24.8 million votes. It also posted a S$76 million net loss on record revenue, because its fuel bill rose seventy-eight per cent. The two facts are the same fact.

stories.kicker: The Meridian Dispatch · The Gulf, day 202
stories.headline: The second gate closes, and the first one stops mattering quite so much
stories.dek: Last weekend this desk reported Saudi crude escaping the Strait of Hormuz by changing ships off Oman. The escape route ran through the Bab el-Mandeb — and over four days in September the Houthis took the whole Yemeni coastline that commands it. Two narrow gates, one hand on both. Oil fell anyway.

stories.kicker: The Little Red Dot · Saturday morning
stories.headline: The air cleared overnight, and Waymo picked the west
stories.dek: Two things landed on Friday while the haze was quietly falling out of the Unhealthy band: Alphabet’s robotaxi arm became Singapore’s third licensed autonomous-vehicle operator, and it is starting at Labrador and HarbourFront. Commercial rides in 2028.

stories.headline: Blocked at the lithography node, Huawei went around it with light
stories.dek: At Huawei Connect on Thursday the company pulled its next AI accelerator forward by three quarters and launched a supercluster that replaces forty-eight thousand optical modules with five and a half thousand optical engines. The chip it cannot buy is still the chip it cannot buy. So it moved the bottleneck to the wires.

stories.kicker: Gear We’re Watching · On sale Tuesday
stories.headline: Half a terabyte of memory in one address space — and nobody has measured it yet
stories.dek: Apple’s new Mac Studio reaches Singapore on Tuesday from S$3,499. The configuration that makes it interesting to a home lab — 512GB of unified memory — does not ship until late October, and no independent review of any version exists.

stories.kicker: Objects & Escapes · Shipping at the end of this month
stories.headline: Esoteric took the motor away from the record and left a magnetic field behind
stories.dek: The T-01 has no belt, no idler and no spindle motor under the platter — the platter is dragged round by induction, with nothing touching it. It is fifty thousand US dollars. A Technics at a tenth of that publishes a better wow-and-flutter figure.

stories.headline: The audience score landed, and it agrees with the critics
stories.dek: Friday’s edition reported Resident Evil opening at three different percentages with no audience number at all. That number now exists: ninety-two, against ninety-six from a hundred and sixty-nine critics. The gap this desk expected did not appear.

stories.headline: It wasn’t the birthday. It was the new school — and it lasts two years
stories.dek: A South Australian reform accidentally ran the experiment everyone needed: two different age cohorts started secondary school in the same month. Twenty thousand students, seven years of census data, and the decline tracks the transition rather than the age.

stories.kicker: The Big Picture · Two central banks, one input
stories.headline: Tokyo raised rates, and the governor said out loud what the week was about
stories.dek: The Bank of Japan went to 1.25 per cent, its highest since 1995, two days after the Fed moved. Asked why so many central banks were tightening at once, Kazuo Ueda answered: the Middle East. Then oil fell on Friday and yields rose anyway.

stories.kicker: The Long Game · Intensity, measured rather than remembered
stories.headline: Twelve minutes a week, if they are the right twelve minutes
stories.dek: A pooled analysis of 147,414 people wearing accelerometers puts about twelve minutes of vigorous activity alongside a hundred and fifty minutes of moderate. Then, in the same month, the same field’s own cardiology body published a statement saying mortality is the wrong thing to be measuring.

stories.headline: Sumo goes on sale at nine this morning, and the marathon shuts in eleven days
stories.dek: Every item below was re-checked against a promoter, a venue or an official ticketing page before it was printed. Two things that were live on Friday are dead this morning, and they are named rather than quietly dropped.

stories.headline: The children learned the word “rate”
stories.dek: A five-hundred-yen sticker sheet for seven-year-olds became, in about twenty months, a speculative asset with a published price index, a counterfeiting problem, criminal prosecutions, school bans and a crash. What it destroyed on the way was a playground gift economy older than anyone now trading in it.
